question: Consumers appear to be complaining more about battery life. Have we seen this before, what did manufacturers do about it, what happened to those products afterwards, and what can we reasonably learn from the evidence?

plan.rationale: Largest material increase in battery complaints (E005).

hypotheses.statement: Products positioned on the need gained more segment share than their launch cohort
Products positioned on the need show lower post-first-sale complaint rates than their cohort

findings.quote: The new Brevik Aero 14 G4 brings all-day battery that lasts up to 17 hours, in a design under 1.3 kg.
findings.observations: P0050: mean segment share 5.66% over first 12 months since first observed sale vs cohort median 4.04% (rank 6 of 16; prediction-interval p=0.354, greater). P0050: 2 month(s) with observed price-and-volume pattern (promotion not confirmed): 2024-M02,2024-M03. P0050: battery complaint rate 8.8% [95% CI 7.5%-10.4%] vs cohort median 8.7% across 15 products in the same months (product-level p=0.593, less); no_detectable_difference.

draft.title: Battery complaints in Premium Thin & Light: evidence investigation

claims.text: In Premium Thin & Light, the battery complaint rate was 6.9% of comments in 2024-M07..2025-M12 versus 4.4% in 2021-M01..2022-M06 (difference 95% CI 2.2% to 2.8%).
Across segments in the recent window: Premium Thin & Light: 6.9% [6.7%, 7.1%]; Budget: 3.8% [3.6%, 3.9%]; Gaming: 3.4% [3.2%, 3.6%]; Mainstream: 3.4% [3.3%, 3.5%]
The baseline rate of 4.4% shows the complaint was present before the increase (status: intensified_long_standing).
The history covers one panel window only, so earlier episodes cannot be checked.

Brevik Aero 14 G4 (P0050) was positioned on the need: "The new Brevik Aero 14 G4 brings all-day battery that lasts up to 17 hours, in a design under 1.3 kg." This is documented positioning, not evidence that the product resolved the problem.
P0050 first observed sale: 2023-M11 (an estimate of market entry, not a verified launch date); reliability usable.
P0050 averaged 5.7% of segment sell-out over its first 12 months, versus a cohort median of 4.0% (rank 6 of 16; p=0.354, BH q=0.354).
P0050 averaged 5.1% of segment sell-out over its first 10 months (sensitivity analysis excluding price-and-volume pattern months), versus a cohort median of 4.0% (rank 6 of 16; p=0.428, BH q=0.428).
P0050 shows an observed price-and-volume pattern (promotion not confirmed) in 2024-M02,2024-M03.
P0050 battery complaint rate was 8.8% versus a cohort median of 8.7% in the same months (p=0.593, BH q=0.593).

Altura Aero 13 G4 (P0113) was positioned on the need: "Introducing the Altura Aero 13 G4: engineered for endurance, with up to 20 hours of battery life so you can work a full day and evening without a charger." This is documented positioning, not evidence that the product resolved the problem.
P0113 first observed sale: 2023-M10 (an estimate of market entry, not a verified launch date); reliability usable.
P0113 averaged 18.1% of segment sell-out over its first 12 months, versus a cohort median of 4.0% (rank 1 of 16; p=0.002, BH q=0.003).
P0113 battery complaint rate was 3.2% versus a cohort median of 8.9% in the same months (p=0.005, BH q=0.010).

Corvane Lumen 14 G2 (P0120) was positioned on the need: "Meet the Corvane Lumen 14 G2: up to 18 hours of battery life and a brilliant OLED display." This is documented positioning, not evidence that the product resolved the problem.
P0120 first observed sale: 2022-M04 (an estimate of market entry, not a verified launch date); reliability unreliable.
Elsari Strike 15 G4 (P0084) is positioned on the need but sits outside Premium Thin & Light, so it is not compared with this segment's cohort.
Consumer signal in Premium Thin & Light: rubric grade Moderate.
P0050: rubric grade Not supported (sales: not_supported; complaints: no_detectable_difference; contradiction: none; grade under pooled FDR: Not supported).
P0113: rubric grade Moderate (sales: supported; complaints: lower_than_cohort; contradiction: none; grade under pooled FDR: Moderate).
P0120: rubric grade Insufficient (sales: not_tested; complaints: not_tested; contradiction: none; grade under pooled FDR: Insufficient).
P0050: possible alternative explanation: Share gains may reflect the observed price-and-volume pattern rather than the positioning.
